modules.name: Security and Data Protection
modules.purpose: Hold the security positions of this scope: encrypted on-device store, server-triggered remote wipe with final-sync attempt, PIN lockout, minimal on-device data scope, honoured suspension states.

modules.name: Coaching Rendering
modules.purpose: Render Prevention Agent cards at the step where they help, in the worker's language, from authored and approved content, with authored Work Instructions as the offline fallback.

modules.name: Gates and Sign-Off Authority
modules.purpose: Enforce the qualification gate on the device with no worker override, handle the offline case through the parked Run, carry sign-off authority including substitute sign-off.

modules.name: Notifications
modules.purpose: Provide an identity-scoped in-application inbox that back-fills on login, carry honest sync-status detail, deliver work-instruction change notices in two tiers, without operating-system push at launch.

modules.name: Worker Lifecycle on Device
modules.purpose: Cover states a worker moves through on the device that are not simply running a Run: pause, step-away and hand-back, substitution handover, at-step certification-expiry enforcement, honoured suspension states.

modules.name: Training Library Viewer
modules.purpose: Be the Frontline viewer of the platform's longer-form training material — online-only, versioned, audited, per-language, creating no production record.

modules.name: Platform Overview and Health
modules.purpose: Answer three questions at a glance — is the platform healthy, are the agents behaving, is anything waiting on the platform team — and carry platform health as first-class.

modules.name: Atom Registry
modules.purpose: Administer the catalog of every atom — what exists, its state, its evals, where it is used, and whether it is enabled platform-wide and per tenant.

modules.name: Core Agents and Composed-Agent Review
modules.purpose: Administer the platform's agent records and stand the platform-level review and eval gate before any tenant-composed agent acts on a floor.

modules.name: Memory Architecture
modules.purpose: Administer the five typed memory stores, retention and redaction policy, the coaching-corpus index machinery, the cross-tenant footprint view, and the Lane-B publication pipeline.

modules.name: Eval Harness
modules.purpose: Hold the platform's hard enablement gate and the scenario set that gates every capability, including the on-device deterministic layer and retrieval quality.

modules.name: Trace Viewer
modules.purpose: Produce, retain and make inspectable the full orchestrator reasoning trace of every agent run, and derive from it the decision record that outlives it.

modules.name: Platform Settings
modules.purpose: Configure platform-wide behaviour across ten categories, hold the global severity catalog, locale packs and versioning policy, render the six enforced invariants as locked, hold the floor register, provide the emergency pause.
key_functions: 23.7.13 Enforced invariants and platform floor register

business_rules.statement: The application manages its own encrypted store regardless of device, because it may run on shared, tenant-owned, or occasionally personal devices and assumes no mobile-device-management is present.
No captured media is reachable from the device gallery, a file browser, a backup, or any other application.
A wipe attempts a final sync of pending captures before erasing, and never erases unsynced work without that attempt.
Compliance suspension: lock immediately, preserve all local data, and show the fixed message "Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved."
Under hard suspension, start no new Runs while letting in-flight Runs complete, capture, sync, compute summaries, and close.
The lock is never delivered by a notification. Suspension arrives as a command and is enforced in the session and capture layers.
No coaching card ever blocks, gates, or delays a step.
A single dismissal raises no supervisor notification; only the Studio-defined repeated-coaching pattern does.
No timing or pace value renders to the worker at any point in this module.
Selection is agentic; translation is never runtime. Coaching content is authored, reviewed content in each supported language and is never machine-translated at runtime.
No interface anywhere in the application permits a worker to override a qualification gate.
The strict posture is the platform default, and the lenient posture records and surfaces the lapse rather than hiding it.
business_rules.enforcement_point: tenant-level setting in the Delivery Operations Hub

business_rules.statement: A gate block while offline parks the Run and offers the worker their other assigned Runs.
A clearance is applied only as a validated command and carries the tenant-defined duration uniformly, not per user.
Clearance expiry re-blocks at the next gate evaluation and never interrupts the step under way.
A supervisor sign-off requires a completed forced sync and is captured through the step-up without ending the worker's session.
Step-level identity re-confirmation is off by default and is enabled per screen in the Standards and Operations Studio only.
No operating-system push notification is registered, requested, or delivered by the application.
In-application notifications cannot be muted by any role.
A notified change is presented on the first screen of the next execution and cannot be bypassed.
No change of either tier interrupts an in-flight Run.
Only in-application and email channels exist; no additional channel is present in the build.
Pausing one worker's session never changes the Run's state for any other worker. Pause is not a Run state.
No interface permits a worker to cancel or terminally complete a Run.
Pre-substitution steps remain attributed to the original worker and cannot be re-attributed on any surface.
Worker-Shift attribution counts each worker who actually performed work exactly once per calendar shift.
No training material is included in any Run package or downloaded to the device.
No authored workflow can create a dependency on library content, and no Run blocks on it.
A viewing creates no Step Execution, Data Capture, or other production record.
No practice or rehearsal mode exists in the build.
Consumption references are picked up from the Work Instruction step context, with no worker-entered part number.
business_rules.applies_to: 22.22 Traceability Duties at the Point of Capture

business_rules.statement: The rework loop records every cycle, append-only, with the original failure permanently retrievable. Nothing is ever overwritten.
Launch genealogy is one level of as-built links plus the full rework history, and no multi-level walk or downstream-consumer hold propagation is implemented.
No unit identifier is ever generated by the device to fill a gap; the terminal safe state is a blocked step with no fabricated identity.
No bill-of-material, recipe, or routing data is held or produced by the application.
business_rules.enforcement_point: scope boundary — external MES master data outside this release

business_rules.statement: No string, instruction, coaching asset, or media item is machine-translated at runtime anywhere in the application.
Publication is blocked in an incomplete locale for authored instruction text.
Gate evaluation, specification checks, and severity classification execute in the native core and are unaffected by disabling or replacing the presentation layer.
Exactly one on-device store holds captured data and queue state.
No state change that matters is conveyed only by sound.
No tenant role can authenticate to the Super Admin platform console under any configuration, including during a support session, a compliance-emergency session, or a JBS grant.
Every mutating action performed by a Platform Engineer is recorded as pending until an Admin approves it, and no such action changes its target object before approval.
Any attempt to change one of the six enforced invariants fails for every account including the root, and the attempt is written to the platform audit log as an attempt on a locked setting.
Every aggregate view renders an as-of timestamp, and a degraded aggregate renders as stale-with-age or unavailable, never as zero and never blank.
No console screen outside a named access session renders record-level operational content for any tenant.

Every command directed at a device or tenant surface renders one of the fifteen defined command states, and no console view renders a command as applied on evidence weaker than a device acknowledgement.
The console being wholly unavailable causes no change to deterministic on-device safety behaviour, agent enablement, or audit commitment on any tenant surface.
An administrative or operational change and its audit event commit in the same transaction, so an action that cannot be audited does not happen. Refusing the action is the guarantee.
No user interface path exists, for any account including the root, to create an atom. Atoms arrive by backend migration.
business_rules.enforcement_point: Atom Registry — the absent create flow

business_rules.statement: Enablement of an atom whose scenarios are pending or failing is refused at submit and again at apply, and both refusals are audit events.
No atom may be registered whose declared side-effects place a model in the deviation-triggering path; registration validation rejects it.
Disabling a detection-class atom has no effect on on-device severity classification or on the Severity 1 automatic hold.
No tenant-composed agent becomes available on any floor without both the tenant's own approval chain and this module's review decision, and without passing sandbox evals.
Tenant-composed action agents cannot be submitted at V1; the Agent Builder offers reasoning composition only.
No agent can widen its own capability scope, alter its own memory grants, change its own type, or self-approve.
Disabling or pausing any agent leaves on-device severity classification and the Severity 1 automatic hold unchanged.
No mechanism exists by which one tenant's memory becomes readable by another tenant or is used as external training data.
business_rules.enforcement_point: architectural isolation, not a permission setting

business_rules.statement: Profile memory holds aggregates only; no individual-level profile record can be created.
No Lane-B proposal is applied without a recorded decision by a Quality Manager or above in the tenant's own Client Command Center.
An undecided Lane-B proposal receives a 30-day stale flag and never expires or is discarded silently.
In-flight runs remain pinned to the workflow version they started on through any Lane-B publication.
No account, including the root, can disable the eval gate or sandbox-before-publish, and both render as ENFORCED in Settings.
Verdicts and their history cannot be edited or deleted by any account.
Every version of the on-device severity-classification table is re-evaluated before it distributes, and a failing version does not distribute.
With models unavailable, agent-behaviour scenarios render as unable-to-run rather than passing, and enablement remains blocked.
Traces are immutable once closed; no account can edit or delete one.
No tenant surface exposes orchestrator internal reasoning; tenants receive a plain-language activity log and an evidence list only.
A run whose trace or decision record cannot be written is recorded as failed or incomplete, never as a successful run.
No tenant configuration can remove or weaken the Severity 1 floor, and an attempt is rejected at entry with the floor stated.
A locale pack with any untranslated key fails publication and names the keys.
A looser-than-floor value is rejected at entry with the bound stated and is never stored. The register rejects; it does not log.
Tightening a bound surfaces non-conforming existing tenant values in a conformance report rather than rewriting them.
The emergency pause has no effect on on-device gates, specification checks, severity classification, or the Severity 1 hold.
Pause and resume are each critical-class and separately approved.
Change class is determined by the setting, never by the operator's role.
Auto-provisioning is off and no public self-signup path exists at V1; onboarding is invitation-driven.
The platform-seeded taxonomy is read-only in every tenant workspace.
No password-only sign-in path exists for any console account.
The compliance-emergency path requires two authorisations, the root and one Admin, and this cannot be reduced to one.
Exactly two notification channels exist platform-wide at every tier: in-app and email.
The per-tenant refresh floor cannot be set below 30 seconds without a recorded scale validation.
Silence on the alerting path is itself detected and raised as an incident.
Every platform scheduler records a misfire with its window rather than skipping silently.
The console never renders a certification claim beyond the stated posture.
Every setting category is an approvable object under the change-approval discipline; a change awaiting approval is visibly pending; nothing applies silently.
Last-write-wins is explicitly NOT used for tenant configuration: the tenant-configuration registry validates and rejects, it does not overwrite and log.
Data is never purged; tombstones mark de-registration and de-authorisation, never data destruction.

Super Admin excludes tenant operational intervention — gate decisions, Lane-B learning approvals, lot releases, and deviation handling belong to the tenant's own Client Command Center; platform staff never take them.
The Super Admin console originates suspension (all three states and their release) and version change only; it never originates lot release, reassignment, or qualification clearance.

decisions.question: Does soft suspension lift on the operator's signal, or automatically on a payment event?
options: Release by explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console, no payment event observed
Automatic exit on payment (per §8.9.2 and Part IX)
decisions.adopted_working_position: release by an explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console, with no payment event observed
decisions.status: adopted working position (adopted 2026-08-14, Option C)
decisions.impact: Determines soft-suspension exit mechanism; no payment integration exists.

decisions.question: How long may a wipe command remain pending, and what happens if the device never returns?
options: (a) indefinite pending wipe with no expiry
(b) tenant-set expiry, command marked expired plus a fleet alert
(c) expiry converts the wipe into lock-on-contact rather than erase-on-contact
(d) two-stage command: device locks immediately on contact, erases only after a successful final sync
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Recommendation is (d) with a tenant-visible pending-age indicator; owner is the client jointly across Frontline and Super Admin.

decisions.question: Does 'server-triggered remote data wipe on logout' mean every ordinary end-of-shift logout, or only a de-authorising logout initiated by the platform?
options: Wipe on every logout (literal §7.11 reading)
Wipe only on a de-authorising logout event initiated by the platform; ordinary logout preserves the queue (reading this chapter adopts)
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required (both readings preserved)
decisions.impact: Literal reading would erase queued captures at every Shared-mode shift handover.

decisions.question: Does the Prevention Agent operate entirely under pre-authorised Studio-authored policy, or must every action agent route through a runtime human gate?
options: §3.7 and §6.6.1 — entirely under pre-authorised, Studio-authored policy; runtime gate only for proposals beyond it
§8.3.2 and §8.3.3 — every action agent routes through a human gate before any effect
decisions.adopted_working_position: gating is declared per agent in the agent record's governance-binding field, whose declared values are `authoring-time policy`, `runtime human gate`, and `none — reasoning agent`; the Prevention Agent carries `authoring-time policy` and no per-event runtime gate
decisions.status: adopted working position 2026-08-14 (Option C); ratification stays with the client's platform team
decisions.impact: Decides whether a coaching intervention inside authored bounds reaches a worker without a runtime human decision.

decisions.question: What happens when the parked Run is the worker's only assigned Run?
options: The worker idles with an honest explanation
The Supervisor is escalated to immediately rather than through the ordinary path
The run no-show timers at plus 15 and plus 30 minutes take over
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Determines device behaviour when a gate block leaves a worker with no other work.

decisions.question: What does 'higher authority' mean for substitute sign-off, given the five roles are additive and non-hierarchical?
options: An identity holding the Quality Manager role may substitute for an unavailable Supervisor (this chapter's reading)
Undefined in the general case — same underlying gap as DEC-PLUS-001
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required, related to DEC-PLUS-001
decisions.impact: Determines who may sign in place of an unavailable Supervisor.

decisions.question: The unit-model engineering paper Traceability_Unit_Model_Solution_v0.1 remains owed and gates the data-model appendix.
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Lot-formation rules determine what the device binds a capture to when a lot boundary is ambiguous mid-shift.

decisions.question: What standardised device profile — make or class, capability tier, and operating-system split — will target fleets standardise on?
options: Name a specific device class
Name a capability tier without naming a make
Accept the working mainstream floor as the commitment
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Sets pre-staging policy, media budget, and performance envelope; recommendation is a capability tier plus a named representative device.

decisions.question: Which dedicated scanners and scanner-integrated devices do the target floors actually use?
options: Client supplies the list
Client supplies representative hardware for testing
Accept camera-based scanning as the launch path with hardware scanning validated post-launch
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Recommendation is the list plus representative hardware, because the camera fallback is materially slower.

decisions.question: How do last-write-wins by device timestamp and server-receipt-time ordering interact in the ordinary (non-skew-flagged) case?
options: Resolve conflicts by server-receipt time rather than device time
Keep device time but route any conflict where the two orderings disagree to the Client Command Center's conflict-and-skew review
Tighten the default skew threshold
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required (newly raised inside E9)
decisions.impact: A device clock fast but within threshold can win a conflict against a capture that happened later in real time.

decisions.question: The capture/screen-element type set for E1.
decisions.adopted_working_position: the adopted seven: measurement entry, photo capture, barcode or Quick Response code scan, checkbox confirmation with its multiplicity setting, digital signature, free text, and dropdown selection, plus none for instruction-only screens
decisions.status: adopted working position of 2026-08-14, both source readings retained in its card
decisions.impact: Fixes the screen-element contract's contents for E1.

decisions.question: Does a reconnecting device upload pending captures before or after pulling pending commands?
decisions.adopted_working_position: Option C — stop class, then captures, then enabling class: stop-class commands land first, then every pending capture uploads with nothing discarded, then the enabling-class commands apply
decisions.status: adopted working position of 2026-08-14, both source readings preserved
decisions.impact: The payload contract must carry a stop-class or enabling-class marker on every command.

decisions.question: What is the storage-full behaviour per platform for iOS and Android when media cannot be evicted before confirmed server receipt?
decisions.status: open — inside engineering design item E6
decisions.impact: Decides what happens when storage runs out before eviction confirmation arrives.

decisions.question: Is per-tenant feature/atom enablement a Platform Engineer change requiring Admin approval (§8.2.2), or a platform-side Admin action (§8.19)?
options: §8.2.2 — Platform Engineer submits, Admin approves
§8.19 — Admin acts directly on platform-side tenant current values including feature enablement
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required, both readings preserved
decisions.impact: Decides Admin authority on per-tenant enablement.

decisions.question: What does a disabled capability mean for work already pinned to a package?
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Governs the fate of in-flight pinned runs when a capability is disabled.

decisions.question: What happens to a deployed composed agent's in-flight runs when it is later deprecated, disabled, or rolled back?
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required; must be resolved before the Agent Builder ships
decisions.impact: Composed-agent deprecation, disablement, rollback and in-flight run treatment.

decisions.question: Does a Lane-B patch bypass the three-stage Author/Reviewer/Release Authority chain?
options: §5.11.1 — no Workflow content reaches the frontline without explicit human sign-off at each of Author, Reviewer, and Release Authority
§5.16.3 and §6.7.4 — an approved Lane-B proposal auto-publishes a patch version with no second approval and no ceremony
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required, both readings stand
decisions.impact: Decides whether a Lane-B patch bypasses the three-stage chain.

decisions.question: What is the authoritative field-by-field assignment of package-borne versus server-only values?
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required; §6.7.4 defers to Part VII, which does not enumerate it
decisions.impact: The package test cannot be applied deterministically until that enumeration lands.

decisions.question: What Recovery Time Objective and Recovery Point Objective apply to the Super Admin platform console?
options: (a) business-hours control plane with a next-business-day recovery objective plus a documented backend path for emergency actions
(b) high-availability service with an objective measured in minutes
(c) split the objective — tight for the emergency subset, relaxed for the rest
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required (new decision raised by this chapter frame)
decisions.impact: Recommendation is (c); the console is the only path to compliance suspension, device wipe, emergency pause, and legal hold.

decisions.question: Where nobody holding the required role is on shift, to whom is an escalation delivered?
options: Platform default delivers to the tenant's Quality Manager role irrespective of shift, marked as a fallback delivery
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required (carried in the source as an open drafting value)
decisions.impact: Governs nobody-on-shift escalation delivery.

decisions.question: Are the record-finish window bounds (default 48 hours, bounds 24 hours to 7 days) settled?
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required; source carries a contradiction about whether the bounds are settled
decisions.impact: Bounds the record-finish window and the run auto-close scheduler.

decisions.question: What is the standing of the 24-month anonymisation model under the no-purge model?
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Reconciles early anonymisation with the platform's no-purge position.

decisions.question: What are the names and codes of the 8 starter Job Types plus 8 Service Types?
decisions.adopted_working_position: the seeded catalogue ships empty at version 1; every tenant creates its own Job Types and Service Type tags immediately at every tier; loading the sixteen later overwrites no tenant-created entry
decisions.status: adopted working position 2026-08-14; names still owed by the client
decisions.impact: The sixteen names appear nowhere in the source and must never be invented.

decisions.question: Governance of the platform-seeded taxonomy.
decisions.status: open — root approves anything touching the taxonomy's governance
decisions.impact: Governs taxonomy authority.

decisions.question: What is the certification answer, including what International Traffic in Arms Regulations is intended to mean?
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required; export-control posture is unresolved-structural
decisions.impact: A genuine ITAR commitment implies US-persons-only operations and a forked deployment topology, colliding with the granted-JBS-access model.

decisions.question: Which compliance standards mandate deletion?
decisions.status: open — Client Decision Required
decisions.impact: Deletion occurs only where a named compliance standard requires it.

decisions.question: Who launches the containment checklist at classification?
decisions.adopted_working_position: the device launches the checklist locally at classification and the Deviation and Containment Agent never triggers it
decisions.status: adopted working position
decisions.impact: Containment work follows the Severity 1 hold and does not trigger it.

decisions.question: The general definition of 'higher authority' given five additive, non-hierarchical roles.
decisions.status: open — referenced as the same underlying gap as DEC-SUBAUTH-001
decisions.impact: Blocks a general rule for substitution authority.

decisions.question: Referenced as an open decision counting against the chapter's coverage figure.
decisions.status: open
decisions.impact: Named in AC-FL-026-5 as one of the decisions that must close before a coverage figure is claimed.

contradictions.description: Soft-suspension exit: §4.2.4 says it lifts on the operator's signal and not on a payment event, and §4.2.1/§8.12 state no payment integration exists, while §8.9.2 and Part IX give the soft-state exit as automatic on payment.
conflicting_values: release by explicit operator signal, no payment event

contradictions.description: §7.11 states remote wipe on logout or de-authorisation; a literal reading would erase the store at every Shared-mode shift handover, contradicting §7.10.7's eviction-only-after-confirmed-receipt rule.
conflicting_values: wipe only on a platform-initiated de-authorising logout; ordinary logout preserves the queue

contradictions.description: Action-agent gating: §3.7 and §6.6.1 say the Prevention Agent operates entirely under pre-authorised Studio-authored policy; §8.3.2 says every action agent routes through a human gate and §8.3.3 labels it 'action, gated'.
conflicting_values: authoring-time policy, no per-event runtime gate
runtime human gate before any effect

contradictions.description: §7.13.3 allows a 'higher authority' to sign in place of an unavailable supervisor, while the platform also states the five roles are additive and non-hierarchical and the audit log records identity rather than 'acting as role'.
conflicting_values: roles are additive and non-hierarchical, so 'higher authority' is undefined

contradictions.description: E9 conflict rule is last-write-wins by device timestamp, while the time-discipline rule makes server-receipt time authoritative for ordering at sync; §7.10.4 reconciles only the skew-flagged case.

Per-tenant enablement authority: §8.2.2 makes atom enablement a Platform Engineer change requiring Admin approval, while §8.19 makes platform-side tenant current-value changes including feature enablement Admin actions.

§5.11.1 requires explicit human sign-off at Author, Reviewer, and Release Authority for all Workflow content, while §5.16.3 and §6.7.4 have an approved Lane-B proposal auto-publish a patch version with no second approval.
conflicting_values: Lane-B patch auto-publishes with no second approval

contradictions.description: Lane-B version classification: a patch under semantic versioning would be v2.1.1, whereas the canonical illustrative republish of the same Workflow is v2.2.0, a minor version requiring the Job Owner's adoption decision.
conflicting_values: v2.1.1 patch, auto-adopts and is tracked
v2.2.0 minor, notified class requiring Job Owner adoption

contradictions.description: §8.6.3 states full traces are retained 24 months while Part X states nothing is purged; reconciled as Derived Clarification that 24 months is the hot-retrievability horizon.
§6.7.4 says the authoritative field-by-field assignment of package-borne versus server-only values is carried in the package contract of Part VII, and Part VII does not enumerate it.
conflicting_values: Part VII does not contain it

contradictions.description: The source carries a contradiction about whether the record-finish window bounds of 24 hours to 7 days are settled.

Export-control posture is unresolved-structural: a genuine ITAR commitment implies United States-persons-only operations and a forked deployment topology, colliding with the granted-JBS-access operating model.
conflicting_values: ITAR commitment with US-persons-only forked topology

contradictions.description: Anonymisation at 24 months for standard tenants sits against the platform's no-purge model; the standing of the anonymisation model under no-purge is unresolved.
conflicting_values: anonymise worker personal data at 24 months

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A security command that cannot be delivered or applied
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The device continues under its last known state, which no surface may misrepresent as the new state
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: A device that never returns; the wipe remains pending under DEC-WIPE-001
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A locked device with all local data preserved; encryption at rest is the operative control rather than the wipe
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reinstatement, reset, or re-enrollment; reconciliation compares what the final sync delivered against what the device held and records the gap

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Command delivery failure (clearance, suspension, substitution, version change)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Command remains queued; device continues under last known state
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Device stays offline; nothing arrives
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Command not applied and not rendered as applied
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconnection and in-order application at safe boundaries

failures_fallbacks.trigger: On-device storage participates in a failure
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Store operates unchanged; media stays inside the application
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Storage-full behaviour is DEC-STORE-001, unresolved
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No media reachable outside the application
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Eviction only after confirmed server receipt plus an integrity check

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Credential paths, step-up, forced sync failure
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Sign-off does not proceed; managed credential reset path
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Offline device cannot complete the forced sync
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: No partial sign-off record is created
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconnection so the forced sync can complete; managed credential reset

failures_fallbacks.trigger: A worker blocked at a qualification gate
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The tenant's posture — notify without blocking under the lenient posture
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Device offline and no clearance can arrive, at which point the Run parks
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The parked Run with all prior captures preserved and queued, and no override path anywhere
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Clearance arrival or certification correction; reconciliation is the DOH grant record against the device's application

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Loss of the agentic layer (coaching selection)
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: The step's authored Work Instructions from the pinned package
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Loss of those instructions, which cannot occur while the Run is executable
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Full execution with authored guidance only
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Agent availability or reconnection; resume after an emergency pause is a separate audited act

failures_fallbacks.trigger: The pinned package itself is the problem
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Package-level rejection at delivery, before the Run is offered as ready
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Mid-Run rendering failure
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A blocked Run with complete, immutable prior captures and never a skipped gated step
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Content correction and republication, or an application release where the defect is in the renderer

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Render cached content honestly; report unavailability rather than an empty list
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: No further rung where nothing operational is at stake
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: An honest unavailability message
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconnection; no queued state exists where nothing was recorded

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Flags recorded and queued; no surface claims the supervisor knows
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Prolonged offline period
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Queued flags preserved locally
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconnection and delivery

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Damaged or unreadable mark, or label not yet applied
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Scan ladder: hardware scanner, then camera, then authorised manual entry
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Screen requires a scan as proof and manual entry is not authorised
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: A blocked step with no fabricated identity — the platform never invents a unit identifier
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Relabelling or scanner remediation

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Handover state composed locally from the run record
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Substitution command cannot be delivered
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Run remains with the original worker's assignment; committed captures stay safe
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Reconnection and command application

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Serve last-known-good aggregate, stamped stale with its age
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Serve per-tenant primary records without cross-tenant roll-up
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Render "measure unavailable" — never a zero, never a blank
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-aggregate on recovery; re-stamp; record the gap window as a telemetry incident

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the transaction with the same idempotency key
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Hold the request at `pending` and surface the failure to the approver
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Change is not applied; object unchanged; request visibly pending
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-drive from the pending request; no partial application is possible by construction

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the whole transaction
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Refuse the action
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: The action does not happen — an action that cannot be audited does not happen
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Operator is told the action was refused and why; nothing to reconcile because nothing changed

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Command dispatch to a tenant surface or device
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Remain queued; retry delivery on the device's own schedule
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Escalate to the platform team with the command's exact state named
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Command remains in a non-applied state and is displayed as such; never rendered as applied
failures_fallbacks.recovery: On reconnection, apply in order with fencing tokens; supersede obsolete commands; record the reconciliation

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Terminate the session immediately and hold the banner until closure is confirmed
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Revoke the underlying grant
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Session closed, no write capability existed, tenant banner cleared only after confirmation
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Post-session record written to both audit streams; compliance-emergency path additionally produces the tenant report

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry the run
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Refuse enablement
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Enablement blocked — the gate fails closed and has no off position
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-run on recovery; record the blocked window; no capability was enabled meanwhile

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry email; in-app remains present and unmutable
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Escalate to the platform team; record per-recipient failure
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Message stays visible in-app; delivery failure is recorded, not hidden
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Re-send with the same audience snapshot; reconcile per-recipient delivery state

failures_fallbacks.trigger: Scheduler misfire — tiering, anonymisation, drift canary, run auto-close
failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Re-run immediately on detection
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Backfill the missed window under supervision
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Job recorded as misfired with its window; nothing executed partially and silently
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Backfill, then verify counts against the pre-window baseline

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Platform continues unattended; tenants unaffected
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Backend tooling for the narrow set of emergency actions, under the same authorisations
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Administration paused; runtime, deterministic safety, and audit continue
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Replay the queued administrative intent; nothing auto-applies on recovery

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Retry validation
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Reject the write with the bound stated
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Write refused; existing value unchanged
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Operator retries after recovery; no out-of-bound value was ever accepted and logged

failures_fallbacks.first_fallback: Structural mitigation — anything that must act immediately acts locally in the safety layer
failures_fallbacks.fallback_failure: Awareness of a change or an escalation reaching the worker later than it would with push
failures_fallbacks.terminal_safe_state: Anything that changes the work is presented as part of starting the work
failures_fallbacks.recovery: Inbox back-fill at next login and sync
